name: Divider
summary: A thin rule that separates blocks of content — full-width, with a label, or a vertical hairline.
lead: ONE custom element — <aha-divider> — defined once, imported unchanged by React and Vue. Shadow-DOM CSS, themed only by --aha-* tokens; a bare tag is a full-width rule, slotted text becomes a centred (or left/right) label, `dashed` swaps to a dashed line, and `orientation="vertical"` is an inline hairline. A label reads as a heading by default (bold, text-default) or, with `plain`, as a quiet regular note. A divider is a static marker with no interactive state, so it carries no motion. Zero drift — the same element, not two look-alikes.
codeNote: Same element, same shadow-DOM CSS → identical render. React (< 19) consumes it via a thin wrapper; Vue binds the custom element natively. The primitive is defined once in @ahaslides-product/design.

props.name: plain
props.desc: Drop the label from heading emphasis (bold, text-default) to a quiet regular note (400, text-secondary)

whenToUse.when: separating stacked sections, list groups, or toolbar items
you only need consistent gaps, not a visible line
the separation reads clearly without any rule — prefer less chrome

opinion.note: A divider is quiet structure — keep it 1px and on the border token. Use a label only when the section genuinely needs naming; reach for whitespace before adding a rule.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — matched to the DS V3 Divider component-set (fileKey MwjvUjVI0HnfwD9EwPXRAy) whose token layer defines divider/colorSplit (between container → --aha-border #E3E3E3) and divider/colorSplitSecondary (inside container → --aha-split #F1F1F1). The matrix: orientation horizontal/vertical, variant solid/dashed, and a slotted label with align left/center/right in heading (bold, text-default) or plain (regular, text-secondary) emphasis — the AntD Divider conventions the DS builds on. Bound entirely to canonical tokens; no measured px/hex literals.
